stories.tag: US - analyst / agentic AI ROI gap
stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: AI Adoption Is Rising Faster Than ROI
stories.body: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI global survey finds 80% of respondents say AI has improved their individual productivity, yet only 37% report a positive EBIT impact — unchanged from 2025 — and just 6% qualify as AI high performers. Large enterprises ($1B+ revenue) are pulling ahead on agents, with 40% now scaling AI agents in at least one function, up from 27% last year, while smaller organizations stayed flat at 22%. The survey also finds that roughly 32% of organizations have decided against buying at least one software product because coding agents now let them build it in-house, directly reshaping the build-vs-buy calculus.
stories.why: The 80%-productivity / 37%-EBIT disconnect is the exact 'pilot stall' story a Graas salesperson can use: individual tool adoption does not equal enterprise value, and the gap closes only when agents are grounded in governed context across workflows. The large-enterprise agent scaling surge (27→40%) signals that Graas's target accounts are already committing budget — the conversation is now about which data foundation makes those agents reliable enough to clear the EBIT bar.

stories.title: For CPG Companies, Agentic AI's Real Payoff Is Growth — Not Cost Cuts (McKinsey, October 2026)
stories.body: A McKinsey article published October 9, 2026, drawing on a survey of 41 senior commercial leaders at predominantly $10B+ revenue CPG companies in the US and Europe, finds that most CPG firms are deploying agentic AI primarily to cut costs and speed up existing work — and are leaving top-line growth on the table as a result. McKinsey argues that agentic AI must be deployed across the full commercial system — innovation, marketing, revenue growth management, and execution — to recapture the lost sales that stem from the increasingly complex CPG-retailer relationship. Time savings are one measure of returns, but the real payoff will be measured in better product availability, pricing, and shelf presence for shoppers.
stories.why: This is a direct opening for Graas: CPG companies are stalling at cost-efficiency pilots because their agents lack the cross-system commercial context (RGM, execution, retailer data) to drive growth. Graas can position its context and data layer as the prerequisite that turns a CPG's cost-reduction pilot into a revenue-recapture engine across the retailer relationship.

stories.title: BCG: 68% of Retailers Expect Agentic Commerce to Have a Significant or Transformational Effect Within Two Years (October 21, 2026)
stories.body: In a survey of 150 retailers and brands published October 21, 2026, BCG finds that 68% of retailers expect agentic commerce to significantly or transformationally reshape how products are discovered and purchased within two years. Eight in ten retailers have already taken a formal position on external AI agents: 42% are making their data discoverable by any agent, 32% are granting access only to chosen agents, and 6% are blocking agents entirely. BCG argues retailers must now win two distinct games simultaneously — the shopper's direct visit and the agent's recommendation — placing new demands on data infrastructure, loyalty programs, and retail media.
stories.why: The 42% of retailers opening their data to any agent represent an immediate infrastructure urgency: if product, pricing, and inventory data is not governed and semantically consistent, agents will surface wrong information and erode trust. Graas can frame its context and semantic layer as the mechanism that makes a retailer's data 'agent-ready' before that 42% window closes competitively.

stories.tag: US - enterprise AI architecture / context layer
stories.title: Atlan Publishes Retail-Specific Context Layer Architecture: SKU Identity and Inventory Truth as the Agent Substrate (2026)
stories.body: Atlan's 2026 retail AI architecture guide argues that a context layer for retail AI must unify SKU definitions, live inventory truth, resolved customer identity, and policy rules into a single governed infrastructure that merchandising, inventory, and customer-facing agents all draw from — instead of each agent rebuilding its own version. The guide highlights a structural failure mode: a product discontinued in an ERP can still appear as orderable in an online store for days because no system propagates the change in real time, and any agent querying a single system inherits whichever version of truth that system holds. Gartner's 2026 data cited in the piece projects that 40% of enterprise applications will include task-specific AI agents by year-end, up from less than 5% in 2025.
stories.why: This is the clearest articulation of why retail AI pilots stall: fragmented SKU, inventory, and identity data means agents hallucinate or contradict each other across channels. Graas salespeople can use this architecture blueprint to show prospects exactly which context gaps — catalog, ERP, POS, CDP misalignment — must be closed before agent ROI materializes.

stories.tag: US - economics / build vs buy AI
stories.title: Gartner: $2.59 Trillion in Global AI Spend in 2026, But Build-From-Scratch Fails 67% of the Time
stories.body: Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% year-over-year increase, with AI infrastructure alone projected at $1.43 trillion. A synthesis of Gartner's RAG total-cost-of-ownership benchmark puts a 'simple' enterprise document-search deployment at $750,000–$1,000,000 in lifetime cost, with the initial build accounting for only 10–20% of that figure, and Gartner projects 70% of in-house RAG builders will see three-year TCO exceed budget by more than 2x by 2027. Vendor-led or partnered AI projects succeed roughly 67% of the time versus approximately 33% for pure in-house builds, which is why most 2026 enterprise budgets now favor buy-and-customize over build-from-scratch for anything outside a core differentiator.
stories.why: The 33% success rate for pure builds — and the hidden TCO blowout — gives Graas a sharp economic proof point for CIOs weighing whether to assemble a context layer internally. Framing Graas as the governed, retail-specific data foundation that eliminates the 2x TCO overrun converts a capability conversation into a CFO-ready business case.
